scheme_name: Out of School Children scheme under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
description:
The Out of School Children scheme is a significant initiative under the Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan. 

It was launched in the year 2001 as part of a nationwide effort to ensure that every child receives an education. 

The scheme specifically targets children who are not enrolled in formal schools. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to bring these out-of-school children back into the education system. 

The government aims to achieve 100 percent enrollment of children in the age group of 6 to 14 years. 

This age group is critical as it falls within the purview of the Right to Education Act, which was enacted in 2009. 

The scheme also aims to reduce the dropout rate among children in this age group. 

The dropout rate in Goa was reported to be around 4.5 percent in the year 2018. 

The scheme provides various benefits to the children who are enrolled. 

These benefits include free textbooks, uniforms, and mid-day meals. 

The monetary value of the mid-day meal scheme is approximately INR 6 per child per day. 

This translates to around INR 1,200 annually for each child receiving meals. 

Additionally, the scheme offers financial assistance for transportation for children who need to travel to school. 

The transportation assistance is capped at INR 500 per month. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme are clearly defined. 

Children aged between 6 to 14 years who are not enrolled in any formal school are eligible. 

There are no specific income criteria for eligibility. 

However, priority is given to children from economically weaker sections. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward. 

Parents or guardians must fill out a registration form available at local education offices. 

The required documents include proof of age such as a birth certificate. 

Additionally, proof of residence is required to establish local residency. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by local education authorities. 

The timeline for the application process is typically open year-round. 

However, it is advisable to apply before the beginning of the academic year in June. 

Disbursement of benefits such as textbooks and uniforms occurs at the start of the academic year. 

The implementing authority for the scheme is the Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan Society. 

This society operates under the Department of Education, Government of Goa. 

The contact details for the Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan Society can be found on the official Goa government website. 

The scheme has seen significant success since its inception. 

As of 2022, approximately 1,500 out-of-school children were enrolled back into the education system through this initiative. 

The government has also partnered with various NGOs to enhance outreach efforts. 

These partnerships aim to identify and enroll children who are not attending school. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted in rural and urban areas to inform parents about the scheme. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crores for the implementation of the scheme in the financial year 2023-2024. 

This budget is aimed at improving infrastructure and providing necessary resources for out-of-school children. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of quality education. 

Special training programs are organized for teachers to handle out-of-school children effectively. 

These programs focus on inclusive education practices. 

The government monitors the progress of enrolled children through regular assessments. 

Feedback from parents and teachers is collected to improve the scheme. 

The scheme aligns with the Sustainable Development Goal 4, which aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education. 

The Goa government is committed to achieving this goal by 2030. 

The initiative has also received positive feedback from various educational experts. 

They have noted the importance of addressing the needs of out-of-school children. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of educational reforms in Goa. 

These reforms aim to enhance the overall quality of education in the state. 

The government is also working on improving the infrastructure of schools. 

This includes upgrading facilities to accommodate more students. 

The Out of School Children scheme is a crucial step towards achieving universal education in Goa. 

It reflects the government's commitment to ensuring that no child is left behind. 

The scheme is regularly reviewed to assess its effectiveness and impact. 

Stakeholder meetings are held to discuss challenges and solutions. 

The government encourages community participation in the implementation of the scheme. 

This includes involving local leaders and organizations in outreach efforts. 

The success of the scheme is measured through various indicators. 

These include the number of children enrolled and their academic performance. 

The government aims to create a sustainable model for education through this initiative. 

The Out of School Children scheme is a vital component of Goa's educational landscape. 

It addresses the pressing issue of educational access for marginalized children. 

The government continues to invest in this scheme to ensure its long-term success. 

In conclusion, the Out of School Children scheme under the Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan is a comprehensive initiative. 

It aims to provide education to every child in Goa. 

The scheme is characterized by its clear objectives, benefits, and eligibility criteria. 

The application process is designed to be user-friendly. 

The government’s commitment to this scheme is evident in its funding and support. 

Through this initiative, Goa is making strides towards achieving educational equity.
